To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the acid-base complex consisting MPA and Tri can serve as a promising proton transport medium in the form of a polymeric blend, and the proton transport mechanism is elucidated using DFT calculations.

proton transport pathways in the MPA-1,2-3-triazole complex and in the polymeric blend of the phosphonic acid and the 1,2-4-triazole polymers have been studied by DFT calculations and proof-of-concept experimental measurements of proton conductivity, FTIR, and (1)HNMR spectroscopy, respectively.
the acid-base complex consisting MPA and Tri shows high conductivity and the polymeric blend consisting PVPA and PVPri shows higher conductivity than NAFION 118.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the proton transport in an acid-base molecular complex and in the polymeric blend of the acid and base polymers and is aimed at the development of proton conductive materials with high conductivity at high temperature and in anhydrotic state.

proton transport mechanisms in an acid-base molecular complex and a polymeric blend, and the results provide insights into proton transport pathways in the complex and the polymeric blend and the role of the 1,2-triazolyl unit.
the proton transport mechanism in an acid-base pair of a phosphonic group and 1, 2, 3-triazol group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proton transport in the MPA/Tri complex and in the PVPA/PVTri blend is a result of the intermolecular proton transfer between the MPA/Ti and PVPA/PVTi, respectively, and the activation energy for this intermolecular proton transport is much lower than that for the intramolecular proton transport in pure Ti or in PVPA, respectively.

the proton transport in the complex of MPA and Tri is mainly governed by the tautomerization of MPA and the fast proton transfer between the two molecules, which was verified by DFT calculations and experimental results.
the proton transport pathways in the MPA and Tri complex are similar to those in the PVPA and PTVTri blend, and the DFT calculations provide an insight on proton transport in these systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proton conductivity of the MPA-Trial complex and polymeric PVPA-PVTri blend was significantly enhanced by the introduction of the acid-base complex, and the DFT calculations were able to provide the molecular level insights into the proton transport mechanism of the MPA and Tri complex and polymeric blend of the PVPA and PTVTri.

we have developed a new acid-base complex for proton transport in which the acid-base interactions between the phosphonic acid group of PVPA and the triazole group of PVTri are much stronger than those in NAFION, and the activation energy of proton transport in the polymeric PVAP-PVTri blend is lower than that in NAFION 115.

the proton transport pathways in the MPA and Tri complex and the polymeric blend of PVTri and PVPA are consistent with the DPT calculations, and the proton transport in the polymeric blend is enhanced by the presence of the 1,2-triazole group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proton transport pathways of the acid-base complexes of MPA-Tri and PVPA-PVTri are similar to those of the acid-base complex of imidazole (Im) and MPA.

the acid-base complex consisting the phosphonic acid and triazole group can serve as a proton carrier and that the proton transport is facilitated by intermolecular proton transfer between the acid and the base.
the combination of the acid and base moieties can be used to increase proton conductivity of polyphosphonic acid polymers.
